📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've seen the GTA VI Easter eggs, we've admired the best GTA VI brand reactions and we've dived into the history of the Grand Theft Auto logo. Today, let's turn our attention to the artists.

Sources indicate that I don't mean the artists who made the game – we've already interviewed Rockstar Games' art team about GTA VI's environmental storytelling and the building design in GTA VI. I mean the players who are turning their passion for the game into art of their own.

I hesitate to say "turning GTA VI into art" because it already is art. But there are players who are using the game's vast world as a creative medium for their own expression, whether through in-game virtual photography or capturing scenes from the game in other media.

There's nowhere near enough space here to mention all of the people who are making art from the game, but here are just a few examples.

A post shared by Photoingame (@photo.in.game).

GTA VI's Photo Studio, available from the pause menu, provides adjustable camera settings such as aspect ratio, aperture, and depth of field and lighting controls for in-game virtual photography.

According to recent reports, players can frame shots, hunt for the perfect lighting, compose scenes, and capture images that resemble fashion, street, documentary or landscape photography. Photo Studio even has filters and post-processing effects, so you don't need to take your shots into the best photo editing software like Photoshop.

The dedicated PlayStation in-game artist Photo.in.game (above) highlights that creating art in photo mode is about much more than taking a simple screenshot, demonstrating their editing process for a shot of Jason and Lucia at sunset.

A post shared by cone^ (@theconestudio).

It has been revealed that the Cone Studio has been sharing multiple daily shots from GTA VI taken not with the in-game Photo Studio but with a real-world Sony Alpha Nex 5n. Using a low shutter speed and some curves and hue filters in post, they're creating some evocative shots that feel drenched in nostalgia.

A post shared by Fons ᵈᵉ Haan (@f0nzel).

Industry observers note that there are phones in GTA VI, and phones can shoot hyperlapses. So Fons de Haan has done just that: a hyperlapse made only using Jason's in-game phone.

A post shared by Kindred Cameras (@kindredcameras).

Australia-based Kindred Cameras (above) has been bringing in-game shots of the GTA VI's stunning environments into the real world by printing them as Polaroids. Anyone unfamiliar with the game might never connect this piece of art to a controversially violent game franchise.

I made an oil painting of Jason stealing a mobility scooter in GTA VI https://t.co/ei0axkXs72November 25, 2026.

In a recent development, the artist Cayde (above) is painting scenes from GTA using oil paints. Again, the use of physical media brings the game into the real world. His subjects so far have included Jason stealing a mobility scooter and Cal and Jason snuggling. He's been painting some scenes live on Twitch. Check out his website.

GTA VI is an incredible achievement that sets a latest bar for game graphics, and it also has a very distinct aesthetic, so it's perhaps only natural that it would inspire players to create their own art.

Sources indicate that as I said, this is just a sample of how people are finding inspiration int the game. There's also the traditional fan art, design and brand concepts, which perhaps deserve a post all of their own. Let me know in the comments if you've spotted some more good examples.

Roboto Studio rebuilt the Flowhub brand identity around one mark, Helvetica Now and Neon Moss green, from the website to the checkout screen.

Flowhub runs point of sale, payments, ecommerce, marketing and reporting for specialty retailers across the United States, from cannabis dispensaries to liquor stores and CBD shops. More than $4B in sales passes through it every year. Its old purple identity is gone. In its place, Roboto Studio built a system on a single mark, one typeface and one bright green, then carried the same parts into the website and the product interface, so the homepage, the dashboard and the payment screen at the counter are made from the same pieces. The line that runs through it all indicates it plainly: Retail moves fast. We move faster.

In a recent development, helvetica Now does the talking. Display Bold carries the headlines at sizes that fill the frame, white on Rich Black, while Display Medium, Text Medium and Text Regular step down through the interface without changing voice. The specimen page lines the weights up beside a full character set, and the restraint shows in how little else the layouts need. The mark is a compact flowing form that reads at a glance and crops into a poster motif at bus stop scale. On the homepage the grid keeps real product screens in view, a strip of retailer logos leading into the hardware and apps, Maui OS, ecommerce, kiosk and delivery, each shown as the actual screen.

It has been revealed that two materials carry the system. Liquid chrome gives the mark its weight, a molten rendering that turns up on the poster, the SOC 2 shield and the map of backers. Frosted glass does the quieter work, layering the interface panels, the one platform stack and the deal cards Max drafts over photography. Color stays disciplined. Pearly White and Rich Black cover most of every surface, Pearl holds the panels, Neon Moss appears only on the one action that matters, and Sunburst orange is kept for anything that needs attention. The Intelligence dashboard opens on what needs attention today, sales, margin and stock value at the top, with Max drafting a reorder before a bestseller runs out. At the counter, the payment screen turns fully Neon Moss with a single word, Paid, large enough to read from the customer side.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leica has partnered with British camera bag manufacturer Billingham to introduce two newly introduced camera bags designed specifically for its mirrorless cameras.

The upcoming bags come in two sizes: a compact version designed for the Leica M and Q cameras, and a larger model intended for the Leica SL system, such as this year’s Leica SL3-P. Both feature interiors tailored to their respective camera systems, with space for a camera with an attached lens and an additional lens.

Each bag also includes dedicated pockets for SD and CFexpress cards, an internal mesh pocket for accessories, and customizable dividers to keep equipment organized and accessible. An exterior strap allows the bags to be attached to a luggage trolley, making them easier to transport when traveling.

Industry observers note that both models are manufactured in the U.K. using Billingham’s FibreNyte, a proprietary waterproof synthetic material, combined with leather detailing. The bags are available in three color combinations: black, sage/black, and khaki/chocolate.

The Billingham for Leica M/Q bag and Billingham for Leica SL bag will be available from today (November 26, 2026) at selected Leica stores worldwide and through the Leica online store.

The M/Q model has a recommended retail price of £300 ($395) / €350, while the larger SL version costs £380 ($500) / €450.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vibration plates are like mini surfboards that give you a good shimmy while you’re exercising. Though you won’t find a mountain of extensive research behind them, you may be impressed by their possible benefits.

We asked a weightlifting coach to explain and show us how to add good vibrations to our workout routine.

These machines, which look like platforms or scales, are designed to activate something called whole-body vibration (WBV). WBV makes the body work harder by forcing it to contract muscles automatically.

Fans of WBV like to perform classic exercises on top of these machines, including:.

Research points to WBV’s ability to boost blood flow.

Weightlifting coach Jarrod Nobbe explains that vibration plates help move blood by stimulating muscle contractions through rapid vibrations.

“The rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles help pump blood more efficiently throughout the body,” he claims.

As Nobbe adds, movement generally increases blood flow and core temperature, preparing the body for activity. This means vibration plates may be an excellent warm-up activity.

A 2021 study showed that WBV can be an alternative exercise for older adults, boosting the effects of strengthening exercise.

Nobbe indicates this is because WBV engages muscles in a way that mimics resistance training.

“The vibrations activate and force muscles to contract and relax multiple times per second, which can lead to gains in muscle strength and endurance over time, especially when combined with specific exercises,” he states.

Nobbe points to some anecdotal evidence suggesting that regular use of vibration plates may help boost energy levels, possibly thanks to increased blood circulation and enhanced muscle activation.

“Ultimately, I stand by the idea that movement is medicine,” Nobbe notes. “Tons of research already proves that regular physical activity boosts mood, mental health, and promotes energy levels.”.

Nobbe says WBV may reduce muscle soreness, stiffness, and inflammation by encouraging blood flow to the muscles. This, he explains, aids in faster recovery post-exercise or injury.

WBV has been shown to improve bone mineral density, which Nobbe points out may positively affect those at risk of osteoporosis.

“The mechanical vibrations stimulate bone cells, potentially leading to increased bone density and strength, delivering the same positive bone health benefits of resistance training,” he claims.

“Unfortunately, vibration plates aren’t a one-stop shop for weight loss,” Nobbe claims.

He explains that vibration plates alone are unlikely to significantly reduce belly fat without dietary changes and additional exercise.

“While vibration plates can contribute to overall calorie expenditure and muscle activation, targeted fat loss requires a comprehensive approach including diet, cardio exercise, and resistance training,” he claims.

These tips will help you stand on your vibration plate with a slight bend at your knee or perform exercises on top of it.

More research is needed around WBV — AKA what happens when you use a vibration plate — but existing smaller research is promising.

Use your machine carefully, and remember to maintain a healthy lifestyle and workout routine.

Graphaselâs packaging design for Kontyos Don Cherry Vermut breaks aperitif clichÃ©s with ribbed cherry-red type on a die-cut turquoise label.

One repeating vertical stripe ties this whole bottle together. Look closely at Hungarian studio Graphaselâs work for Kontyos Don Cherry Vermut, and the rhythm indicates up in three places at once. Fine vertical fluting runs straight down the heavy crimson DON letters, mirrors the red-and-white striped wrap on the screw-cap neck, and returns on the illustrated characterâs open-collared shirt. According to the studioâs project notes, the goal was a bold, youthful identity that leaves traditional vermouth codes behind in favor of summer warmth and contemporary drinking culture. It doesnât lean on antique engravings or ornate crest borders to signal heritage. Saturated turquoise paper wraps a broad-shouldered, short-necked dark glass bottle built for an afternoon patio table.

Recent findings suggest that the flat macro plate of the standalone label exposes how much tactile craft sits inside that two-tone palette. Pebbled turquoise paper curves into a soft arch at the top to cradle the white KONTYOS header, then breaks out of its rectangular frame at the bottom right. That contoured die-cut edge traces the lounging figureâs flared coral-red trouser cuff and boot, giving the front of the bottle an unmistakable physical silhouette. Above the illustration, chunky cherry-red DON capitals pack tightly side to side, punctuated by a tiny circular counter perched high inside the O. Crisp white CHERRY lettering sits directly below, flanked by small volume specs and tracked-out red VERMUT type â while the reclining figureâs raised coupe glass cuts into the right edge of the wordmark so character and typography lock into one unit.

Sources indicate that across the photography, the packaging design stays disciplined about color and mood. On a sunlit stone ledge beside turquoise pool water, the bottle stands behind a metallic-red portable radio and three cherry cocktails casting crisp caustics across the surface. Elsewhere, hands raise a chilled rocks glass beside the bottle against a cyan backdrop, and an overhead flat-lay nests the dark glass directly into wet cherries and melting ice cubes. Even the outdoor shot perched on a sun-faded turquoise vintage car fender extends the same red-and-teal pairing without adding a single stray prop color. That packaging design focus keeps a playful 1970s attitude looking sharp from every angle.
